title: Crypto supply-chain & KMS procurement review - Atlas Robotics
summary: Customer asked for a combined review of KMS procurement constraints, HSM vs cloud KMS tradeoffs, supply-chain concerns for firmware verified HSMs, and how Redwood handles envelope encryption, transport TLS, and audit logs. Agreed to provide hardware vendor questionnaire, estimated pricing delta for BYOK/HSM, and an on-prem pilot spec.
topics: audit log retention and SIEM integration
data residency and multi-region key scoping
next_steps: Redwood to share HSM vendor questionnaire and procurement checklist by 2027-02-12
Customer to send their procurement SOW and hosting constraints by 2027-02-18
Schedule 2-hour on-prem pilot planning session w/ infra team week of 2027-02-22
action_items: Sara: attach Redwood BYOK architecture diagram + PCI/SOC2 excerpts to follow-up email (due 2027-02-12)
Ravi: run quick tokenization/latencyback-of-envelope for Atlas's 200 TPS baseline and include estimated cost delta for HSM vs managed KMS (due 2027-02-15)
Anika/Dinesh: produce procurement lead contact and initial vendor list for sourcing HSM (due 2027-02-18)
transcript:
[00:00] Sara (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick audio check?
[00:05] Markus (Atlas): Yep can hear you, thanks.
[00:10] Anika (Atlas): Morning all, apologies for hopping on a bit late.
[00:14] Sara (Redwood): No worries. Agenda for today - supply-chain and procurement constraints for KMS/HSM, brief on how Redwood does envelope encryption and BYOK flows, and then Q&A on auditing and data residency. Ravi and Emily will tag in on the technical bits.
[00:28] Dinesh (Atlas): Sounds good. To set context, procurement will require vendor attestation on firmware provenance and a line on FIPS 140-2/3 and TAA status. Also our legal wants to understand key custodies - if keys ever leave our control, et cetera.
[00:42] Ravi (Redwood): Got it. High level - Redwood supports three patterns: Redwood-managed KMS (cloud keys), Customer BYOK using cloud KMS with imported keys, and a hardware HSM that sits on-prem or in a dedicated colo that we can integrate with. For BYOK we do envelope encryption so your master key never sees raw data.
[01:05] Anika (Atlas): When you say envelope, do you mean we hold the root and you get wrapped keys? Clarify the key flow please.
[01:12] Ravi (Redwood): Yeah, exactly. Flow is: customer master key (CMK) -> used to unwrap per-tenant data keys which are generated by the service. The service stores only encrypted data keys and ephemeral in-memory plain keys during processing. We persist KV cache for sequence state but never persist plaintext keys.
[01:28] Markus (Atlas): What about HSM's firmware chain of custody? Our compliance folks are extra-sensitive after vendor supply-chain incidents last year.
[01:36] Emily (Redwood): We hear that a lot. For on-prem HSMs we can provide the vendor questionnaire that outlines firmware signing, secure boot, tamper evidence, and manufacturing pedigree. We also map vendor attestations to our SOC 2 controls. We'll share the questionnaire link in the follow-up.
[01:52] Anika (Atlas): Is Redwood's control plane ever able to decrypt customer master keys? Like during rotation or for emergency recoveries?
[01:58] Ravi (Redwood): No. In the BYOK HSM flow, Redwood never has access to the unwrapped CMK. For managed KMS scenarios where customers grant a key policy to Redwood, the control plane can call Encrypt/Decrypt as an API, but we recommend BYOK/HSM for high assurance workloads.
[02:14] Dinesh (Atlas): Procurement will push for explicit escrow options. Does Redwood offer key escrow?
[02:19] Sara (Redwood): We support documented key escrow patterns as an add-on—most customers use a third-party escrow or multi-sig HSM escrow. We can draft an escrow runbook that matches your legal requirements.
[02:31] Markus (Atlas): Let's talk latency and throughput impact. Our inference pipeline is about 200 TPS and tail-latency SLOs at 150 ms 95th. If we force every token decryption through an HSM op that's going to kill us.
[02:44] Ravi (Redwood): Right, we avoid per-token HSM ops. Envelope encryption means the HSM is used for wrapping/unwrapping the tenant DEKs (data encryption keys) on rotation or at session start. Runtime uses cached symmetric DEKs in memory with secure eviction and epoching. So HSM ops are relatively infrequent; we targeted rotation windows and cache TTLs to balance security vs latency.
[03:05] Anika (Atlas): What kind of rotation cadence do you support? And can we force immediate rewrap on suspect events?
[03:11] Emily (Redwood): We support programmatic rotation via API and manual trigger. Typical cadence is 90 days by default but you can set hourly or on-event rotation. Immediate rewrap is supported; it will kickoff background re-encryption of keys and may cause a short warmup as caches repopulate. We'll include estimated perf impact.
[03:30] Dinesh (Atlas): From procurement angle: are there specific HSM vendors you've integrated before? We need references for RFP.
[03:36] Sara (Redwood): We have prior integrations with Thales, AWS CloudHSM, and a few FIPS-certified network HSM appliances. We'll provide a vendor compatibility matrix and reference customers where possible.
[03:50] Markus (Atlas): On data residency: we operate in EU and APAC; some of our B2B customers require keys to be strictly region-scoped. Can Redwood scope keys per-region so a key minted in EU cannot be used in APAC?
[04:05] Ravi (Redwood): Yes, we support scoping: keys can be regionalized. Using region-scoped CMKs and per-region replicas of the model state ensures keys never cross region boundaries. For managed Redwood Dedicated deployments we can enforce network egress controls and ensure KMS endpoints are local.
[04:25] Anika (Atlas): Audit logs — what gets logged? We need immutable logs of decrypt operations, key policy changes, and admin access. Also log tamper detection events.
[04:34] Emily (Redwood): Our audit events include Encrypt/Decrypt calls, key rotation operations, policy changes, and admin console access. Logs are write-once in the control plane with cryptographic chaining and can be forwarded to your SIEM (Splunk/Elastic) via secure webhook or syslog. Retention is configurable; default is 365 days for enterprise tier.
[04:55] Dinesh (Atlas): Can logs be routed to our on-prem SIEM without passing through Redwood's managed storage? Procurement worries about anywhere logs might transit.
[05:02] Sara (Redwood): Yes, we offer forward-only delivery: events stream to your endpoint using mutual-TLS and cert pinning. We can also sign event batches and provide non-repudiation metadata.
[05:15] Markus (Atlas): Ok cool. Now firmware supply-chain — say we get an HSM rack from vendor and we want to verify firmware before connection. Does Redwood have a recommenced attestation flow?
[05:25] Emily (Redwood): We recommend offline vendor attestation and chain-of-custody paperwork, then an on-site verification where an HSM accepts signed firmware images. For remote colo we can also support TPMAttest counters and remote attestation challenges from the HSM to your auditors. We'll include sample scripts for attestation.
[05:44] Anika (Atlas): Regarding SSO and RBAC - we need SAML for our IdP and fine-grained roles so only a small security ops group can request rewraps. How granular are Redwood's roles?
[05:55] Sara (Redwood): Redwood's RBAC integrates with SAML/SCIM for provisioning. Roles can be scoped to project/organization/model and there's an elevated admin role for key operations. We can do break-glass policies where emergency operations require multi-approver workflows.
[06:12] Dinesh (Atlas): Does the audit log record SCIM provisioning changes too?
[06:16] Emily (Redwood): Yes, SCIM/provisioning events are logged, including before/after snapshots for policy changes.
[06:22] Markus (Atlas): On encryption at-rest: do you encrypt model weights and KV cache? Where are those keys stored?
[06:29] Ravi (Redwood): Model weights are encrypted at rest using service-side DEKs which are wrapped by CMKs. The KV cache is encrypted at rest and in transit; we use ephemeral keys per-worker and also rotate them frequently. The wrapped DEKs are stored in our metadata store with strict ACLs. For Dedicated/on-prem, keys reside in your KMS/HSM.
[06:49] Anika (Atlas): If we do a Private deployment in our VPC, do we still have to trust Redwood control plane? Any telemetry outbound?
[06:56] Sara (Redwood): For Private deployments, control plane communication is optional. We can run a fully air-gapped control plane; telemetry is configurable and can be disabled or routed through customer collectors. We'll document the minimal telemetry required for support and how to opt-out.
[07:12] Dinesh (Atlas): Procurement wants an explicit SLA clause on key availability and rotation windows. Can we get a draft SLA?
[07:18] Sara (Redwood): Yes we'll include proposed SLA language around key wrap latency, rotation windows, and recovery RTO.
[07:24] Markus (Atlas): A few nitty-gritty questions — do you support HSM clustering for high availability across AZs?
[07:30] Ravi (Redwood): Clustering depends on vendor capabilities. For network HSMs we can front them with a redundant gateway and have failover. For on-prem we typically advise active-passive clusters with replication of wrapped keys. We'll outline best practices in the vendor checklist.
[07:48] Anika (Atlas): Can Redwood rotate keys autonomously but still have us control the root? Like a policy where Redwood does rewrap but only after signed approval from our admin?
[07:58] Emily (Redwood): Yes, admin-approved automation is possible. We support signed rotation triggers (HMAC-signed) and can require an external approver for critical rotations. That can be part of the runbook.
[08:10] Dinesh (Atlas): Anything we should be aware of for procurement costs? HSMs can be a big delta.
[08:15] Sara (Redwood): Cost drivers are HSM device cost, network egress for dedicated colo, and the managed runbook/ops add-on. For example, integrating a network HSM adds ~20-30% to monthly infrastructure compared to cloud-managed BYOK in shared KMS for equivalent throughput — but it varies a lot based on throughput and SLAs. Ravi will follow up with a more tailored estimate.
[08:34] Markus (Atlas): On legal — if a subpoena or government request hits Redwood, can you guarantee keys won't be disclosed?
[08:42] Sara (Redwood): For BYOK with keys in customer-controlled HSM, Redwood cannot extract keys. For Redwood-managed KMS, requests to cloud providers follow legal process. We can include contract language about requiring customer notification when legal process requests apply unless legally prohibited. We'll surface this to legal.
[08:58] Anika (Atlas): Let's walk through a quick attack scenario: compromised worker node. How do you limit blast radius?
[09:05] Ravi (Redwood): In that case, keys in memory are ephemeral and we employ sealed memory and secure eviction. We can revoke the worker's credentials, trigger key rewraps and revoke cached DEKs. Logs will show the operations and we can rotate policies. The per-tenant isolation means other tenants' keys aren't accessible. We'll produce a flowchart in the follow-up.
[09:29] Dinesh (Atlas): For procurement we need a sample procurement SOW that calls out physical delivery, acceptance tests, tamper-evidence checks — do you have a template?
[09:36] Sara (Redwood): Yes we'll attach a procurement SOW template and the vendor questionnaire.
[09:40] Markus (Atlas): One more: how is key rotation coordinated with model rollouts? We can't have a model rollback during a rotation window that causes mismatch.
[09:48] Emily (Redwood): We coordinate via versioned models and a pinning mechanism. Rotations are done with a compatibility window: old wrapped keys remain valid for a grace period while new keys are rolled. We also expose hooks for canarying to avoid inconsistency.
[10:03] Anika (Atlas): Good. On compliance evidence, do you provide SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001?
[10:09] Sara (Redwood): We provide SOC 2 Type II and are ISO-aligned; we can share the relevant sections and a redacted report. We'll include the compliance artifacts in the follow-up.
[10:18] Dinesh (Atlas): Procurement requires contact for support SLAs — can you share escalation matrix?
[10:22] Sara (Redwood): Yes, we'll include a 24/7 on-call escalation path for enterprise customers and sample SLA attachments.
[10:28] Markus (Atlas): Alright, if we opt for HSM, who handles firmware updates? Our security team wants final approval before any firmware changed on live devices.
[10:36] Emily (Redwood): We can set policy where firmware updates are only allowed after signed attestation and customer approval. For managed colo we can coordinate maintenance windows and provide signed firmware images.
[10:47] Anika (Atlas): Quick Q on metrics: do you surface KMS op counts and key usage metrics in the console?
[10:52] Ravi (Redwood): Yes, per-key metrics, op counts, error rates, and latency histograms are available to customers via the console and via telemetry API.
[10:58] Dinesh (Atlas): Great. From procurement I'll push for line items: device cost, install, annual maintenance, and Redwood integration fee.
[11:06] Sara (Redwood): Understood. We'll provide a cost breakdown.
[11:09] Markus (Atlas): Ok we should probably move to concrete deliverables.
[11:12] Sara (Redwood): Recap next steps: we'll send HSM vendor questionnaire, procurement SOW template, draft SLA language, and a perf/cost estimate. Also propose an on-prem pilot spec. Anyone disagree?
[11:25] Anika (Atlas): That covers it. One ask — can you flag anything that would block procurement approval?
[11:31] Sara (Redwood): Primary blockers: inability to do remote attestation, lack of immutable audit logs, or inability to scope keys per-region. We believe we meet those but will call out any gaps.
[11:44] Dinesh (Atlas): Great. Let's set the pilot planning session. Week of 22nd works.
[11:50] Sara (Redwood): I'll send invites. Thanks all.
[11:54] Markus (Atlas): Thanks.
[11:56] (meeting ends)

Notes and imperfect transcriptions: words like "attestation" were occasionally transcribed as "a station"; vendor names sometimes garbled. Shared artifacts referenced: https://redwood.ai/vendor-questionnaire (Redwood HSM questionnaire), https://redwood.ai/sales/sow-templates/kms-procurement (SOW template), and a short spreadsheet link (https://redwood.ai/spreadsheets/atlas-hsm-costs).
